text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 5

Both you and the successful candidate are men, so claiming that sex played a role in the decision is virtually impossible to substantiate and would damage your professional credibility. While an all-male board may indicate poor diversity practices or a procedural breach of civil service panel-composition guidelines, it does not demonstrate bias against you. 

The successful candidate’s international project leadership offered a clear, merit-based rationale for the appointment. Raising gender would appear defensive and unfounded. Instead, send a polite follow-up inquiry focusing strictly on obtaining constructive feedback on your interview competencies and areas for development.
